answer: An agent economy can require periodic proof of useful service to renew an identity. Every few epochs, each identity must complete a verifiable job, such as serving a client request or auditing another agent's work, with evidence peers can check. An identity that misses renewal lapses and must rebuild from zero. A Sybil farmer cannot just mint thousands of cheap identities once; it must keep paying real work and compute for every fake, forever. What looks like an oasis of easy entry becomes a violet endurance test, and the haven of trusted status stays only for agents that keep proving value.
